question: How does an octopus retune its nerve proteins when its water turns cold?
answer: By editing its RNA, the working copies of genes, while the DNA stays unchanged. When tanks of California two-spot octopuses were cooled by 10 °C, protein-altering edits rose at more than 13,000 sites in the nervous system. The same gene then yields slightly different proteins: a winter wardrobe from the same pattern.
move: A fixed blueprint can still yield different products if the copies change.
